findings.highlight: I'll force you down on my bed.
findings.evidenceJa: 容赦なく病院に連れ帰るからね
findings.explanation: Takayanagi warns that if Youko shows any sign of illness, he will take her straight back to the hospital without mercy. The English invents a sexual threat to force her onto his bed.
findings.japanese:
「とにかく今日は大人しくしてなさい。
少しでも具合が悪そうに見えたら、
容赦なく病院に連れ帰るからね」
findings.todokanai: "Either way, be good today. If I see even a hint of your health failing, I'll force you down on my bed."

findings.highlight: I doubt the beginning of the concert will be a quiet one.
findings.evidenceJa: 今のところ落ち着いた滑り出しに見えないでもなかった
findings.explanation: Despite the tickets selling instantly, the currently only seventy-percent-full hall could be seen as a calm start. The English says Haruki doubts the opening will be quiet, reversing his provisional assessment.
findings.japanese:
それでも、チケット販売時の瞬殺ぶりから考えると、
今のところ落ち着いた滑り出しに見えないでもなかった。
findings.todokanai: But considering all the noise that was made when the tickets were still on sale, I doubt the beginning of the concert will be a quiet one.

findings.highlight: being forced to sit by and watch these two restless adults go after each other
findings.evidenceJa: 意地を張ったり逡巡したりして、かえって悪辣な大人たちを楽しませるのも癪だった
findings.explanation: Haruki leaves because stubbornly refusing or hesitating would only entertain the two wicked adults teasing him. The English says he cannot bear watching the adults attack each other.
findings.japanese:
意地を張ったり逡巡したりして、
かえって悪辣な大人たちを楽しませるのも癪だったので、
俺はそそくさと席を立った。
findings.todokanai: Remaining stubborn with her, or being forced to sit by and watch these two restless adults go after each other was far too unbearable to me, so I got off my seat and left.

findings.highlight: we kept ignoring each other
findings.evidenceJa: すれ違いを繰り返してた二年前
findings.explanation: Two years earlier Haruki and Setsuna repeatedly missed or misunderstood each other while trapped in an unresolved relationship. 'Kept ignoring each other' turns crossed signals into deliberate mutual avoidance.
findings.japanese:
俺たちが中途半端な関係のまま、
すれ違いを繰り返してた二年前…
雪菜は、二度ほど俺たちの前から姿を消した。
findings.todokanai: Two years ago when our relationship was uncertain, we kept ignoring each other… Setsuna disappeared twice.

findings.highlight: in an attempt to find her
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜を力ずくで見つけ出してきた
findings.explanation: On each prior disappearance, Haruki mobilized a large search and forcibly succeeded in finding Setsuna. The English reduces the achieved result to an attempt.
findings.japanese:
その度ごとに、俺は周囲の人たちを巻き込んで
大規模な捜査網を引き、
雪菜を力ずくで見つけ出してきた。
findings.todokanai: Each time I involved everyone around me, and organized a search on a large scale in an attempt to find her.

findings.highlight: would usually be forced to join in
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の無茶に乗っかって、一緒に無茶をしてくれた
findings.explanation: Io and Takeya willingly bought into Haruki's recklessness and acted recklessly alongside him. The English says they were forced to participate, reversing the loyalty being mourned.
findings.japanese:
そして、そういう時いつも、
俺の無茶に乗っかって、
一緒に無茶をしてくれた…
findings.todokanai: And they would usually be forced to join in on my absurd efforts during times like those…

findings.highlight: she has told me as little as she could get away with, but now I have to force it out of her
findings.evidenceJa: 今までは、一を語るだけだった意志の疎通も、十も二十も語って聞かせるしかない
findings.explanation: Their former mutual understanding needed only one part spoken; now Haruki must explain ten or twenty parts to make himself understood. The English instead accuses Io of withholding information and makes Haruki force it out of her.
findings.japanese:
今までは、一を語るだけだった意志の疎通も、
十も二十も語って聞かせるしかない。
findings.todokanai: Up until now, she has told me as little as she could get away with, but now I have to force it out of her.

findings.highlight: My five calls earlier got transferred to voicemail
findings.evidenceJa: さっきまでは、５コールくらいで留守番電話に移行してた
findings.explanation: Earlier each call transferred to voicemail after about five rings. The English says five separate calls were transferred, obscuring why the presently continuing ring count proves Setsuna's phone is on.
findings.japanese:
さっきまでは、５コールくらいで
留守番電話に移行してたのに、
今はずっとコールが続いている。
findings.todokanai: My five calls earlier got transferred to voicemail, but now my call is continuing.

findings.highlight: I won't sleep in peace.
findings.evidenceJa: 困るよ、俺
findings.explanation: Haruki says simply and personally that if Setsuna does not go home, he will be troubled. The English invents sleeplessness and turns the direct admission of emotional stake into a practical consequence.
findings.japanese: 「雪菜が帰らなかったら…困るよ、俺」
findings.todokanai: "If you don't go home, Setsuna… I won't sleep in peace."

findings.highlight: where I went on a date with a boy for the first time
findings.evidenceJa: わたしが、初めて男の子をデートに誘った場所
findings.explanation: Setsuna identifies the karaoke bar as the first place where she invited a boy on a date. The English instead calls it her first date with a boy, erasing her initiative and changing her romantic history.
findings.japanese:
「南末次の、カラオケ屋…
わたしが、初めて男の子をデートに誘った場所」
findings.todokanai: "The karaoke bar in Minami-Suetsugu… where I went on a date with a boy for the first time."

findings.highlight: picking a song right before the time was up just to sing for a few extra minutes
findings.evidenceJa: 終了時間までぎっしり予約で埋めてあって、しかも店内電話が鳴ったとき、ぴったりと最後の曲の後奏に入って
findings.explanation: Setsuna had packed the reservation through closing time and timed the set so the final song entered its outro exactly when the room phone rang. The English invents an attempt to steal extra minutes and loses the joke about her meticulous selfishness.
findings.japanese:
終了時間までぎっしり予約で埋めてあって、
しかも店内電話が鳴ったとき、
ぴったりと最後の曲の後奏に入って。
findings.todokanai: Singing for as long as the reserved time would allow, and even picking a song right before the time was up just to sing for a few extra minutes.

findings.highlight: "For three years, we kept missing one another. For two years, we were in each other's arms."
findings.evidenceJa:
「三年間、ずっとあなたとすれ違って、
二年間、ずっとあなたと触れあってきたんだよ？」
findings.explanation: For two years Haruki and Setsuna kept in contact/touched one another; 'were in each other's arms' makes the whole span exclusively physical-romantic — Their bodily and emotional entanglement is explicit in the following lines.
findings.japanese:
「三年間、ずっとあなたとすれ違って、
二年間、ずっとあなたと触れあってきたんだよ？」
findings.todokanai: "For three years, we kept missing one another. For two years, we were in each other's arms."

findings.highlight: ineffective at leaving an impression on you
findings.evidenceJa: わたし、そんなにあなたに影響を与えられてなかった
findings.explanation: Setsuna asks whether she truly had so little influence on the person Haruki became. 'Leaving an impression' suggests memorability rather than the formative interpenetration of their five-year history.
findings.japanese:
「わたし、そんなにあなたに影響を与えられてなかった？
そんなに…あなたと絡み合うことはできなかったの！？」
findings.todokanai: "Was I that ineffective at leaving an impression on you? Was our bond… so fragile that you could just tear it off like that?"

findings.highlight: but just barely
findings.evidenceJa: 震えてはいたけれど、儚さは取り払われていた
findings.explanation: Setsuna's voice still trembles, but its fragility has been stripped away. 'But just barely' says the voice itself barely persists, nearly the opposite of its recovered firmness.
findings.japanese: 震えてはいたけれど、儚さは取り払われていた。
findings.todokanai: Her voice was shaking, but just barely.

findings.highlight: let out my thoughts, only to have her watch as I try to stop myself from saying too much
findings.evidenceJa: ただ一方的に自分の思いを募らせ、そして必死で思い留まるくらいは許して欲しかった
findings.explanation: Haruki wants permission only to let his feelings accumulate unilaterally inside him and desperately restrain himself from acting on them. The English invents him voicing those thoughts and Setsuna watching his attempted self-censorship.
findings.japanese:
ただ一方的に自分の思いを募らせ、
そして必死で思い留まるくらいは許して欲しかった。
findings.todokanai: I only wanted to one-sidedly let out my thoughts, only to have her watch as I try to stop myself from saying too much.

findings.highlight: her words enter my head, and one after another, they wreak havoc
findings.evidenceJa: 否定の言葉が、次から次へと頭の中に浮かび、そして、次から次へと頭の中で潰していく
findings.explanation: Words denying Setsuna's self-condemnation rise one after another in Haruki's mind, and he crushes each one before speaking it. The English makes Setsuna's words invade and damage him, erasing his deliberate silence.
findings.japanese:
否定の言葉が、次から次へと頭の中に浮かび、
そして、次から次へと頭の中で潰していく。
findings.todokanai: One after another, her words enter my head, and one after another, they wreak havoc.

findings.highlight: one that is exactly like her to make
findings.evidenceJa: 本当に雪菜らしい、偽悪の言葉だった
findings.explanation: Haruki recognizes Setsuna's apology as characteristically 偽悪: language that falsely casts herself as the villain. The English calls the interpretation merely like her, omitting the explicit mechanism of self-villainization.
findings.japanese:
その雪菜の謝罪は、
あまりにも一方的な解釈に囚われた、
本当に雪菜らしい、偽悪の言葉だったけど。
findings.todokanai: Setsuna's apology came from a one-sided interpretation, one that is exactly like her to make.

findings.highlight: with a complete lie
findings.evidenceJa: 最低の偽善で応えた
findings.explanation: Haruki answers Setsuna's false self-condemnation with what he calls the worst hypocrisy: assuring her Kazusa will play while seeing evidence that she needed him present. A lie is not the same moral category as self-serving hypocritical consolation.
findings.japanese:
それでも、敢えて俺は、
その言葉に、最低の偽善で応えた。
findings.todokanai: Even so, I answer her words with a complete lie.

findings.highlight: to never do anything that would get in the way
findings.evidenceJa: 護るための障害となるようなことは、一切約束しないって、新しい誓い
findings.explanation: Haruki vows never to make any promise that could become an obstacle to protecting Kazusa. The English says he will never perform an obstructive action, losing the passage's recursive distinction between vows and the freedom to break expectations.
findings.japanese:
そして、護るための障害となるようなことは、
一切約束しないって、新しい誓いを立てた。
findings.todokanai: And so I made another vow, to never do anything that would get in the way of protecting her.

findings.highlight: Be my reason to work as hard as I can.
findings.evidenceJa: 俺が頑張れるように、一生、俺の負担になってくれ
findings.explanation: Haruki asks Kazusa to remain his burden for life so that carrying her will give him strength to strive. The English keeps the motivation but omits the deliberately paradoxical request that she burden him.
findings.japanese:
「俺のために、ずっと役立たずでいてくれ。
俺が頑張れるように、一生、俺の負担になってくれ」
findings.todokanai: "Be useless, for my sake. Be my reason to work as hard as I can."

findings.highlight: Something that is of absolutely no use to Kazusa
findings.evidenceJa: かずさは自分の中に何も生み出さない。けれど、俺の中に強いエネルギーを灯してくれる
findings.explanation: Kazusa produces nothing within herself, but lights a powerful energy within Haruki. The English changes internal production into usefulness to Kazusa and drops the contrast between emptiness in her and generation in him.
findings.japanese:
かずさは自分の中に何も生み出さない。
けれど、俺の中に強いエネルギーを灯してくれる。
findings.todokanai: Something that is of absolutely no use to Kazusa, yet gives me a powerful energy.

findings.highlight: keep saying things like that and I actually might
findings.evidenceJa: 今からそんな縁起でもないこと考えてたって
findings.explanation: Haruki protests that there is no point thinking such ill-omened thoughts already. The English has him say Kazusa's words might actually cause his early death.
findings.japanese:
「お前なぁ…
今からそんな縁起でもないこと考えてたって」
findings.todokanai: "Hey… keep saying things like that and I actually might."

findings.highlight: I'll do everything I can to make something of myself
findings.evidenceJa: あたしは絶対やり遂げてみせるからな
findings.explanation: Kazusa defiantly vows she will absolutely follow through on killing herself after Haruki dies and challenges him to stop her if he can. The English turns this into the life-affirming promise to make something of herself.
findings.japanese:
「それこそ、何とでも言え、だ。
あたしは絶対やり遂げてみせるからな。
…止められるものなら止めてみろ」
findings.todokanai: "And you can say whatever you want. I'll do everything I can to make something of myself… and if you think you can stop me, I dare you to try."

findings.highlight: if we could have managed to keep the balance between us
findings.evidenceJa: 三人の平均を取れば、だけどな
findings.explanation: Kazusa jokes that the wedding future was happiest only when the three people's happiness is averaged: Setsuna and Haruki gain much, while Kazusa suffers at the organ. The English replaces this explicit arithmetic joke with maintaining relationship balance.
findings.japanese:
「そんな未来が、三人にとって一番幸せだったんだ。
………三人の平均を取れば、だけどな」
findings.todokanai: "That future would have been the happiest future for the three of us… only if we could have managed to keep the balance between us."

findings.highlight: a smile that could tear herself apart
findings.evidenceJa: 俺にとっては、とんでもなく身勝手だけど、身を引き裂かれる笑顔
findings.explanation: To Haruki, Setsuna's withdrawal is outrageously selfish and her smile tears him apart. The English makes the smile tear Setsuna herself apart and omits Haruki's pained accusation of selfishness.
findings.japanese:
そして俺にとっては、
とんでもなく身勝手だけど、身を引き裂かれる笑顔。
findings.todokanai: And in my eyes, she wore a smile that could tear herself apart.

findings.highlight: our check-out from this place
findings.evidenceJa: 俺たちの精算
findings.explanation: Setsuna begins the final settling of accounts between herself and Haruki. The English literalizes 精算 as checking out of a location, erasing the emotional reckoning.
findings.japanese: 俺たちの精算を…始める。
findings.todokanai: She begins our check-out from this place.

findings.highlight: Snow that only ever fell during times of hardship and sorrow.
findings.evidenceJa: 辛いこと、悲しいことを時期限定で埋め尽くす、白い幕
findings.explanation: Snow is the white curtain that appears at their crossroads and blankets painful and sad things only temporarily. The English says it falls only during hardship and sorrow, moving 時期限定 from the duration of concealment to the occasions of snowfall and losing the warning that the cover will melt.
findings.japanese:
いつも俺たちの分岐点に現れ、
辛いこと、悲しいことを時期限定で埋め尽くす、白い幕。
findings.todokanai: The curtain of white that always appeared during the crossroads of our lives. Snow that only ever fell during times of hardship and sorrow.

findings.highlight: I can no longer be with Setsuna. That's what she herself has said to me.
findings.evidenceJa:
俺は、もう、
雪菜の側に寄り添えない。
自分で、そして雪菜に言ってもらったじゃないか。
findings.explanation: Haruki says both he himself and Setsuna have told him he can no longer stay beside her; the English credits only Setsuna — His self-imposed separation is explicit throughout the scene.
findings.japanese:
俺は、もう、
雪菜の側に寄り添えない。
自分で、そして雪菜に言ってもらったじゃないか。
findings.todokanai: I can no longer be with Setsuna. That's what she herself has said to me.
